quote.translation: And August Faust says: "If the concrete filling-out of the content of all intra-worldly existence is still to be understood conceptually in any way, it becomes clear that an extremely contentless abstract concept such as possibilitas logica (logical possibility) is precisely what is indispensable" (August Faust, Der Möglichkeitsgedanke, II, S. 59).

quote.translation: From the ultimate standpoint, which admits logical possibility and with it disjunctive contingency, it is contingent that this clover has four leaves and not three, and contingent that Mount Asama is a volcano and neither a fault-block mountain nor a fold mountain.

quote.translation: It is also contingent that Toyotomi Hideyoshi was born in Nakamura in Owari, and not in Kyōto, or Ōsaka, or anywhere else.

quote.translation: Leibniz, stating that innumerable worlds were possible, holds that there could have been a world in which Sextus Tarquinius was born in Thrace and became the happiest of men, the object of the veneration of the whole people, a world in which he was born in Corinth and grew old in mediocrity, loved by his fellow citizens, a world in which he was born in Rome, violated another man's wife and became an exile, and besides these innumerable worlds containing Sextuses of every kind and in innumerable fashions (Sextus de toute espèce, et d'une infinité de fa- çons) (Leibniz, Théodicée, III, §§ 414-416, Opera philos., ed. Erdmann, pp. 622-624).
